sourceEvidence.label: MP-LogManager Web editor rendering and modal source review

assessment.summary: Repeated dynamic HTML sinks support one shared safe-rendering boundary rather than independent escaping patches.

nonNegotiables: Preserve the JSON schema and top-level data structure.
Preserve the GAS API contract and Google sync semantics.
Preserve iPhone native full-document Journal selection.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
The small Vanilla JavaScript application can accept one additional local utility module.
Vendored DOMPurify 3.4.14 remains the approved sanitizer dependency.

opportunities.title: Centralize untrusted DOM rendering
opportunities.summary: Place every intentional Markdown-to-HTML conversion behind one sanitizer and construct other untrusted content as text nodes with programmatic event bindings.
opportunities.diagnosis: The application has a safe Task Markdown path, but equivalent controls are dispersed or absent in Journal print, record lists, diagnostics, and notifications.

evidence.claim: printJournal inserts marked.parse output directly into print-content.innerHTML without DOMPurify.
renderTasks interpolates persisted identifiers, category, priority, and due date into HTML and inline event handlers.
renderJournalList interpolates persisted identifiers and dates into HTML and inline event handlers.
Connection diagnostics, caught error messages, and toast messages are concatenated into innerHTML.
Because safe rendering is owned by one feature rather than a shared boundary, later HTML surfaces can omit or diverge from the sanitizer policy.

desiredInvariants: Every Markdown-to-HTML conversion passes through one DOMPurify-backed fail-closed renderer.
Every other user, Drive, GAS, or network-derived string reaches the DOM through textContent or an equivalent text-node API.
Persisted identifiers never become executable inline event-handler source.
Sanitizer absence, lack of browser support, or exceptions produce inert text rather than unsanitized HTML.

options.title: Add guards at each current sink
options.summary: Patch Journal print and escape or validate each current interpolation while retaining feature-owned rendering code.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A local DOMPurify call directly protects the observed print sink.
Local escaping and identifier validation protect the current Task card template.
Local escaping and identifier validation protect the current Journal list template.
Each diagnostic and toast interpolation receives a local text treatment.
Control ownership remains distributed, so future sinks can still omit a guard.

tradeoffs.assessment: The known sinks can reject active content, but the application retains several independently maintained policies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the attack corpus against every patched sink and search all innerHTML assignments for untrusted values.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local string escaping and one print-time sanitizer call add bounded work on existing render paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare Task/Journal list render time and Journal print preparation before and after the patch.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option retains existing string templates and adds only temporary escaped strings.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record heap growth while repeatedly rendering a large Task and Journal list.

tradeoffs.assessment: Malformed values become less likely to break the current DOM, although mismatched local policies remain possible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Render malformed identifiers, null metadata, and sanitizer failures across all current surfaces.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new module appears, but reviewers must continue auditing every sink independently.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure review effort by checking whether one search can establish all rendering invariants.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small local patches are easy to stage and revert with no data or API migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Ship each sink patch separately and confirm the existing visual snapshots.

residualRisks: A new feature can introduce another unsanitized sink.
Different local sanitizer configurations can drift.
Inline event source remains attractive unless every list is fully refactored.

workPackages: Patch each current sink and add per-sink regression cases.
acceptanceCriteria: The known attack corpus remains inert on every current dynamic HTML surface.
migrationNotes: Keep the existing Task Markdown sanitizer while other sinks are patched.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the individual sink patch while retaining v2.3.3 Task Markdown sanitization.

options.title: Adopt one shared safe-rendering boundary
options.summary: Centralize sanitized Markdown, use DOM text construction elsewhere, and remove persisted identifiers from inline event source.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Journal print must migrate to the shared Markdown boundary.
DOM construction and closure-bound listeners remove metadata and identifiers from HTML source.
DOM construction and closure-bound listeners remove Journal identifiers from HTML source.
Diagnostics and toasts use typed nodes with dynamic values assigned as text.
One Markdown policy and a text-by-default DOM convention reduce future control drift, though they do not enforce a browser-level policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: One fail-closed Markdown boundary and text-only DOM construction remove the repeated source-to-innerHTML pattern from the reviewed paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run one shared attack corpus across Task Markdown, Journal print, lists, diagnostics, and toasts; audit remaining innerHTML assignments.

tradeoffs.assessment: DOM construction may trade one large HTML parse for multiple element operations; the small expected list size suggests modest impact, but no benchmark exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark 0, 100, and 1,000 record renders against v2.3.3 and investigate regressions above 20 percent.

tradeoffs.assessment: Temporary template strings shrink while node creation and listener closures grow; the net effect depends on record count.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare heap snapshots after repeated 1,000-record render and teardown cycles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Malformed persisted values can no longer reshape markup or executable attributes, and sanitizer failures have one defined fallback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test null, unexpected-type, malformed-ID, parser-error, sanitizer-error, and unsupported-browser cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reviewers can inspect one sanitizer policy and a smaller set of intentional HTML sinks; no service or deployment component is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document the allowed sinks and confirm a repository search maps each one to constant or sanitized content.

tradeoffs.assessment: Task and Journal list construction changes more substantially and requires careful visual and event regression coverage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Migrate one surface at a time, preserve visual snapshots, and retain the v2.3.3 sanitizer until Task parity passes.

residualRisks: A future developer can still bypass the convention because CSP and Trusted Types are not in scope.
Sanitizer defects remain part of the trusted computing base.
Third-party Markdown and editor CDN versions remain a separate supply-chain concern.

workPackages: Migrate Task and Journal Markdown callers.
Replace dynamic card, diagnostic, and toast templates with typed DOM construction.
Run security, visual, event, performance, and offline regression coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Every reviewed untrusted value is inserted as text or shared-sanitizer output.
No persisted identifier is interpolated into inline executable code.
The full attack corpus remains inert and positive Markdown remains readable.
migrationNotes: Retain tactical v2.3.3 Task sanitization until the shared boundary passes parity tests.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the staged surface migration and cache version; no stored data conversion is required.

opportunities.recommendation: Under the balanced, small-application constraints, use the shared boundary because its reviewability and recurrence reduction justify the moderate list-render refactor.
